items.headline: Hormuz Day 87: Nuclear Enters Deal Framework — Iran Agrees 'Never Pursue Nuclear Weapons' + Negotiate Enrichment Suspension + HEU Removal; Tasnim 'One or Two Clauses Still Persist'; No Khamenei Statement; Brent $102-106 Intraday; WPA 4 Days
items.summary: The structural state of the deal has materially upgraded since the morning filing. Axios and CNN, sourcing a senior administration official, report that Iran has agreed in principle to three nuclear commitments: (1) never pursue nuclear weapons; (2) enter negotiations on suspending its uranium enrichment program; and (3) negotiate removal of its stockpile of highly enriched uranium. These are the most specific and significant nuclear concessions attributed to Iran since the conflict began — and they represent a fundamental shift in the deal architecture from the morning's characterization of 'nuclear excluded from current framework text.' The 60-day window described by the senior official is now framed not as a blank deferral but as a structured negotiation period with defined subject matter: enrichment suspension and HEU disposal. The implications for the congressional constraint are meaningful but incomplete. The 52 senators and 177 House members who signed the zero-enrichment letter demanded immediate cessation of enrichment as a deal condition — Iran's commitment to 'negotiate over suspension' is a commitment to negotiate, not a commitment to zero enrichment now. The gap between 'agree to negotiate' and 'zero enrichment as of deal signing' remains real and politically significant. Critical uncertainties persist. Iran's semi-official Tasnim news agency confirmed overnight that 'differences over one or two clauses of the possible memorandum of understanding still persist' — the specific clause(s) in dispute are not publicly identified but may include timing of sanctions relief, control mechanisms over the strait, or the sequencing of enrichment suspension vs. sanctions removal. Mojtaba Khamenei has issued no public statement throughout the Memorial Day cycle. His silence is now approaching 72 hours since Trump's 'largely negotiated' declaration — sustained Supreme Leader silence at this stage could reflect internal deliberation or IRGC-hardliner resistance to the nuclear framework language specifically. The Iranian FM has issued no formal text confirmation of the described nuclear commitments. The Fars news agency dismissal remains the last published IRGC-aligned institutional signal. Trump officials told Axios the deal may take 'days' — not hours, not imminent — suggesting continued negotiation activity into Tuesday May 26 at minimum. Brent crude traded in the $102-106 intraday range on Memorial Day, closing below the $105-107 pre-announcement baseline but without the $15-20 conviction collapse that would signal full market pricing of a closed deal. The range is consistent with market-conditional belief that has slightly strengthened since the morning open. The analytic anchor for the evening: the nuclear framework inclusion is the most important structural development since Day 1. But it is a framework commitment to negotiate, not a signed zero-enrichment agreement, and it lacks Supreme Leader validation.

items.summary: Kevin Warsh enters the evening of Day 11 without a public statement. His swearing-in ceremony on May 22 — 'I will lead reform-oriented Federal Reserve' — remains the only public utterance of his chairmanship. The most material economic development of Memorial Day is the report of nuclear commitments now included in the Iran deal framework: Iran's agreement to 'negotiate over' suspension of uranium enrichment and removal of HEU stockpile, combined with a commitment to never pursue nuclear weapons, structurally strengthens the disinflationary pathway without confirming it. The logic: a deal that includes nuclear commitments — even negotiation-to-negotiate language — is more likely to hold as a durable settlement than a deal that leaves nuclear to an indefinite parallel track. A more durable settlement has a higher probability of leading to Hormuz normalization, which is the precondition for any energy-price relief. The probability-weighted disinflationary outlook has improved materially since the morning, even though the pump-price timeline has not changed: Hormuz reopening still requires transit normalization (days-weeks post-announcement), supply-chain normalization (weeks), and retail price response (weeks to months). The earliest retail pump-price relief from a deal signed today would still arrive in late June at the earliest. Brent crude traded $102-106 intraday on Memorial Day — consistent with conditional-to-elevated deal probability, still well above the $85-90 level that would signal full market conviction of a closed deal. The EIA short-term energy outlook projects $106/b for Brent in May-June — the intraday Memorial Day range is at the lower end of that forecast, suggesting the market is beginning to price deal probability at a discount to the baseline. The April CPI print at 3.8% YoY (energy +17.9%, gasoline +28.4%) remains the pre-deal inflation baseline against which any crude-driven disinflation will be measured. PPI runs at 6.0% annualized. The June FOMC is 22 days out; the December rate hike probability remains near 40% based on current CME positioning. Warsh's first public economic statement — whenever it arrives — will now need to address both the deal-conditional disinflationary pathway and the nuclear framework's implications for durable energy price relief. His silence has compounded through the highest-stakes diplomatic development of his chairmanship. The communication gap is acute.

items.summary: The War Powers Act situation is structurally unchanged from the morning: the 90-day hard deadline arrives May 29, four days away, and Congress returns tomorrow from Memorial Day recess with three calendar days before the threshold. The most significant new development of the day — nuclear commitments reportedly entering the deal framework — does not change the WPA analysis. The WPA threshold requires physical cessation of hostilities: Hormuz must be open, the naval blockade must be lifted, and US military operations must have ceased. As of Memorial Day evening, Hormuz is physically closed, the naval blockade is active, and neither condition has changed. Even if a formal deal text with nuclear commitments were signed tomorrow, May 26, implementing Hormuz reopening would require transit normalization negotiations (days), which precedes physical strait opening (days to weeks). The physical WPA threshold will not be crossed before May 29 regardless of what deal text is signed before then. The administration's 'hostilities terminated' posture — asserting the ceasefire pause stopped the WPA clock — does not survive Day 90 plain-text scrutiny. At Day 90 on May 29, the Iran war will definitionally operate outside any credible statutory basis. House Republican leadership has explicitly scheduled the next war powers vote for early June — after the deadline. No Senate 8th resolution is scheduled. The bipartisan House majority (Rep. Golden confirmed yes, six Republicans) is real but dormant. The deal's nuclear framework development may generate a new administration legal argument — that a 'framework agreement' including nuclear commitments constitutes a pathway to cessation sufficient to satisfy congressional authorization — but this is constitutionally novel and not established by precedent or statute. The first legislative day after Congressional return is tomorrow, May 26: three calendar days before May 29. Any pre-deadline emergency session, White House Counsel statement, or DOJ OLC guidance is a highest-priority watch signal for the May 26-28 window.

Post-recess City Council action is required; no emergency session has been announced. The compound PNW stress vector — peak fire risk + measles accelerating + record gas prices + labor supply uncertainty + municipal fiscal strain — is at its highest coherence since the conflict began.

analyst_summary: Memorial Day Evening, May 25, 2026 — Hormuz Day 87, Naval Blockade Day 44, Project Freedom Pause Day 20, WPA Day 26 Past Statutory Deadline / 4 Days to 90-Day Hard Deadline May 29, Warsh Day 11. Vibe 4 — firmer than morning, with materially strengthened upward lean. The defining development of the evening cycle is the Axios/CNN reporting that nuclear commitments are now reportedly inside the deal framework: Iran has agreed in principle to never pursue nuclear weapons, to negotiate suspension of its uranium enrichment program, and to negotiate removal of its HEU stockpile. This is the most important structural evolution of the deal architecture since Day 1 of negotiations. The morning brief characterized nuclear as 'excluded from current framework text'; the evening brief characterizes it as 'reportedly included with 60-day structured negotiation window.' That is a significant upgrade. But the upgrade does not yet move the vibe to 5 for three reasons: (1) Iran's commitment is to 'negotiate over' suspension and HEU removal — not immediate zero enrichment — leaving the congressional constraint (52 senators, 177 House members demand zero enrichment at signing) unmet; (2) Tasnim confirms 'one or two clauses still persist' — the deal is not closed; (3) Mojtaba Khamenei has issued no public statement since Trump's 'largely negotiated' declaration on Saturday — 72+ hours of Supreme Leader silence is the most significant outstanding uncertainty of the cycle. Vibe 4 holds. The Khamenei binary remains the single highest-priority geopolitical signal: confirmation of nuclear framework = vibe 5; hardening or rejection = vibe 3. Brent crude held $102-106 intraday — no conviction collapse, but below the EIA $106/b baseline, consistent with the market beginning to price deal probability at a discount to the supply-shock baseline. The WPA 90-day hard deadline is 4 days away; nuclear deal text evolution does not change this — Hormuz is physically closed and the physical threshold for cessation will not be crossed before May 29. Congress returns tomorrow. Oregon fire season is Day 18 with Memorial Day marking the peak human-ignition risk day; Level 1 restrictions and BLM Day 12 restrictions are operative; Trout Creek Fire (43 acres, near Sisters) is the confirmed season-opening fire; the prepositioning window is 7 days and closing with the first federal response opportunity arriving tomorrow. The compound PNW stress vector — peak fire risk, measles school window at ~2 operative days, record gas prices, green card labor supply uncertainty, Portland fiscal strain — is at its highest coherence since the conflict began. Vibe 4.
